_doc: Legacy REST resource-route status and body-code table for the command
conformance resource-route shim (Task 07.0 subtask 09). It is the single
data-driven source the shim uses to (a) assert a corpus step's declared
rest_resource.status is the real legacy status for that command+outcome (so
a corpus author cannot silently weaken a status, plan.md C3) and (b)
translate a legacy REST error body code into the envelope error vocabulary
before the shared matcher compares error.code.
Provenance: success statuses are copied from the HTTP characterization
tests tests/unit/http/02_endpoint_matrix_characterization.cpp and
03_method_and_error_characterization.cpp; the error_status map and the
error-table legacy_code_to_envelope promotions are copied from the
legacy_rest_* columns of src/commands/error_codes.cpp (all_error_infos),
which are themselves copied verbatim from statusForAppError/codeForAppError.
The field-level 400 codes (invalid_enabled, invalid_expires_at,
invalid_redirect_type, invalid_tags, invalid_campaign, invalid_metadata,
invalid_argument, and the stats invalid_bucket/invalid_timestamp) are the
per-field codes the REST body decoder in src/http/handlers/link_handlers.cpp
emits before the registry runs; they all mean the envelope's invalid_field
(the same failure class the generic/registry transport reports), so they map
to invalid_field for cross-transport parity (subtask 09 implementation step
3). invalid_url/invalid_slug/reserved_slug stay distinct envelope codes. The
error status is
the same for every command because there is a single error table, so it is
hoisted to error_status rather than repeated per command as the subtask spec
example shows; 14_rest_resource_corpus.py tests this table against both the
shared catalog status table and a live server so neither can drift.
